\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Compute the minimum possible value for \( x \).

Give the minimum value of x as an exact expression using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals (no trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions, and no approximations).

Let

\[
a=\frac yx,\qquad b=\frac zy,\qquad c=\frac xz.
\]

Then \(abc=1\). Dividing the last two equations by \(xyz=3\) gives

\[
(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=\frac{40}{3},
\]
\[
(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

Let \(S=a+b+c\) and \(P=ab+bc+ca\). Since \(abc=1\),

\[
(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=2+S+P=\frac{40}{3},
\]
\[
(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=P-S=\frac{4}{3}.
\]

Solving,

\[
S=5,\qquad P=\frac{19}{3}.
\]

Thus \(a,b,c\) are the roots of

\[
t^3-5t^2+\frac{19}{3}t-1=0,
\]

or

\[
3t^3-15t^2+19t-3=(t-3)(3t^2-6t+1).
\]

So

\[
\{a,b,c\}=\left\{3,\;1+\frac{\sqrt6}{3},\;1-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}\right\}.
\]

Since \(y=ax\) and \(z=abx\), we have

\[
xyz=a^2b x^3=3
\]

so

\[
x^3=\frac{3}{a^2b}.
\]

To minimize \(x\), we maximize \(a^2b\) over ordered distinct pairs \((a,b)\) from the set above. The maximum is attained at

\[
a=3,\qquad b=1+\frac{\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Hence

\[
x_{\min}^3
=\frac{3}{9\left(1+\frac{\sqrt6}{3}\right)}
=\frac{1}{3+\sqrt6}
=\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}}
\]
